proposal.reveal_strategy: Reversible acquisition probe, designed as an instrument rather than a twenty-seventh geometric guess. The evaluator's standing conclusion is correct: permuting contact XY, jaw alignment and pre-close entry path is exhausted across iterations 14-26, and the live hypotheses are host-side. So this probe is built to discriminate between them. Contact height 47.5 mm sits 2.42 mm above this frame's own table_z and 2.7 mm above the run's lowest estimate, well inside the already-used 43.0-62.5 mm band, so Z is deliberately not the changed variable. What changes is jaw alignment to yaw 75, untried in a run that has used -75, -60, -30, -20, 0, 10, 15, 36, 45, 60, 85 and 90, and a lengthened 30 mm open-jaw in-plane out-and-back pass directed outward toward the free cuff edge and back to the exact anchor. The discriminative value: a 30 mm plane-level pass across a free hem must ruck the cloth if the fingertips are physically there, so a visible ruck without a retained pinch would isolate closure actuation, while a twenty-sixth pixel-identical silhouette hardens the reach or execution fault into the only surviving explanation. Disclosures, in advance and against interest. (1) Grounding overshoot: (492.88, -201.74) is 69.8 mm from the Molmo image-left sleeve hint, failing the historical 40 mm gate by 29.8 mm and my own stage-1 band of 40-55 mm by 14.8 mm. I am proceeding rather than abandoning because the proximity gate is not the only evidence available and is weaker here than reproducibility: this measurement lands 11.9 mm from three R087 readings whose Camera C hold-checks independently confirmed the jaws over image-left sleeve fabric, and 187.8 mm from the validated torso centre, so the balance of evidence puts it on the named sleeve. That reasoning is falsifiable and should be scored: if this iteration's hold-check shows the jaws over torso or shoulder rather than the sleeve lobe, then the reproducibility argument is wrong, left_sleeve must not be credited, and the result must not be counted against sleeve contact geometry, exactly as in iterations 15, 16, 19, 21, 23 and 26. (2) The lookup budget is exhausted and the 2 mm anchor rule binds the pre-close move, so re-selection is impossible and I will not fabricate a coordinate. (3) Prediction: I expect null. Standing escalations, unchanged and blocking. Twenty-six closes have driven position_pulse 850 to 0 with no arrest and mechanical_grasp_detected false, and close_gripper accepts only an empty args object, so jaw width, pinch force, closure speed and partial-close width cannot be commanded; a host answer on whether any parameterised, force-limited or partial close exists is a precondition, not a request. Every telemetry sample remains simulated:true sharing one timestamp per iteration (03:45:58.128 through 07:13:33.794), so whether a real arm and gripper are mechanically in the loop is unresolved, and twenty-five probes with a pixel-identical silhouette fits actuation that never physically occurs better than twenty-five independently mis-aimed grasps. An instrumented touch-down recording height at first contact is still needed, or a definitive statement that it is unavailable; the witness ladder has been run above, at and below the plane estimate and yields only a lower bound. Path shaping reuses the rule that produced controller-valid IK in iterations 23, 24 and 26: one constant yaw at every waypoint, staged transit at z 120 then z 80, no wrist rotation during translation. Structure is strictly reversible with zero net lateral displacement, two purely vertical hold checkpoints at +20 mm and +35 mm, reversal to the exact contact pose, release there, and a vertical retreat; home is omitted only because the 12-action cap is reached, and the vertical retreat leaves the tool clear above the garment. No transport, no laydown. For context only and not part of this iteration, the eventual credited left_sleeve motion would carry the lobe inward toward the torso centreline, roughly 80-110 mm, laying the cuff over the chest print.

The overlay draws the uniform reference grid over the whole mask at a 48 px stride, with a dense cluster of markers over the image-left lobe and its cuff edge. decision.opening_strategy: Keep current_step left_sleeve; the ledger is empty and nothing has been folded. Two lessons from the physical record drive this iteration. First, iteration 26 failed on grounding rather than geometry: R075 measured 64.97 mm from the Molmo hint and the witness view put the jaws over upper torso/shoulder fabric, so the seam-bead relief hypothesis was never actually put to the sleeve, and eight of twenty-six iterations have now been lost to a mis-grounded anchor. The first requirement is therefore to stop losing iterations to grounding, which means choosing the reference with the best measured record of landing on the named sleeve rather than the one whose drawn marker looks most appealing. Second, the evaluator is right that permuting contact XY, jaw alignment and entry path has been exhausted across iterations 14-26 and that the live hypotheses are now host-side: a commanded-TCP-to-fingertip offset, a Z pipeline fault, a close that cannot be parameterised, or motion that never physically executes. Since the contract still requires a probe, I make this probe an instrument aimed at those hypotheses instead of a twenty-seventh geometric guess. The design keeps grasp height inside the already-used band so Z is not the changed variable, and changes jaw alignment to an untried yaw and lengthens the open-jaw in-plane pass to about 30 mm directed outward across the free cuff edge. The value is discriminative rather than acquisitive: a 30 mm pass at plane level across a free hem must ruck the cloth if the fingertips are truly there, so a visible ruck without a pinch would isolate closure actuation, while another pixel-identical silhouette hardens the reach or execution fault into the only surviving explanation.

decision.expected_observation: Three distinguishable outcomes. (2) The diagnostically valuable partial: no pinch, but one or more contact-sheet tiles show the cuff or lobe rucked, puckered or dragged along the pass direction and then relaxing. That would prove for the first time that the fingertips physically reach cloth, and would localise the fault to closure actuation alone. (3) Twenty-sixth clean null with the silhouette pixel-identical from tile 1 to tile 16, which is what I expect. Combined with sub-plane passes at plane -1.6 and -4.6 mm in iteration 20, a 30 mm pass that fails to move a free cuff edge bounds any commanded-TCP-to-fingertip discrepancy well above 10 mm or means the arm is not physically executing the commanded motion. safety_notes: Strictly reversible: out-and-back pre-close pass returning to the exact anchor, release at the exact contact pose, zero net lateral displacement, no post-close transport and no fold laydown.

Keep contact height a small margin above this frame's own table estimate and never below the lowest table estimate of the run; the fifteen readings in this region span 44.80-60.76 mm, so the plane cannot be trusted to better than about 16 mm.
Stage the descent through a high transit and an intermediate height before the plane-level approach so a mis-measured plane cannot drive the fingertips into the table at speed.
Hold one constant yaw at every waypoint with no wrist rotation during translation; wrist rotation during translation caused two consecutive IK rejections earlier in this run.
The 30 mm pass runs outward toward the free cuff edge and away from the torso, so any successful pinch takes sleeve ply rather than capturing torso fabric and pre-empting a later fold step.

If the stage-2 measurement for R087 re-indexes off the sleeve, as the 48 px stride bug has done four times on R082 and R087, abort rather than fabricating a coordinate or substituting a convenient region; the lookup budget is one call and the anchor rule binds the pre-close move.

A well-grounded 30 mm open-jaw pass at plane +2.4 mm across a free cuff edge that produces zero cloth motion cannot be attributed to region, yaw, entry path or ply thickness.

Stop issuing geometric permutations entirely. Iterations 14-27 have now covered interior mid-lobe ply, edge-crossing lines, corner straddle, off-cloth edge capture, throat capture by sweep, diagonal wedge under the free hem, cuff double ply, seam-band relief, pure vertical arrival, and yaw at -75, -60, -45, -30, -20, 0, 10, 15, 36, 45, 60, 75, 85 and 90. A twenty-eighth permutation carries no information.

Treat a commanded-TCP-to-fingertip offset, a Z-pipeline fault, or an arm that never physically executes the motion as the confirmed leading diagnosis. Open jaws have now arrived or passed in-plane at roughly plane +10, +2.9, +2.5, +2.4, +2.3, +1.9, +1.5, -1.6 and -4.6 mm across iterations 18-20, 22, 24, 26 and 27, spanning about 20 mm of absolute Z on both sleeve and torso ply, with no cloth response of any kind. Jaws at or below the cloth plane must disturb it; the discrepancy exceeds 10 mm, or the motion is not occurring.

Escalate closure actuation as a confirmed blocker, twenty-second consecutive iteration: twenty-six closes have driven position_pulse 850 to 0 with no arrest and mechanical_grasp_detected false, and close_gripper accepts only an empty args object, so jaw width, pinch force, closure speed and partial-close width cannot be commanded. A host answer on whether any parameterised, force-limited or partial close exists is a precondition, not a request.

Resolve whether a real arm and gripper are mechanically in the loop before iteration 28. All twelve samples are simulated:true sharing one timestamp (07:23:13.109), matching 03:45:58.128 through 07:13:33.794. Twenty-six probes with a pixel-identical silhouette fits actuation that never physically occurs far better than twenty-six independently mis-aimed grasps.

Provide an instrumented touch-down recording height at first contact, or state definitively that it is unavailable. table_z 45.08 mm is the sixteenth mutually inconsistent estimate in this region and now the lowest of the run (spread 45.08 to 60.76 mm), and height_above_table 18.27 mm on visibly flat single ply is not plausible. The witness ladder has been run above, at and below every estimate and yields only a lower bound.

If the host requires further iterations under the probe contract, change what is instrumented rather than where the jaws go: permit a commanded initial jaw state or a pre-close close/translate/open sequence so contact footprint can be tested, or expose a touch-down height. Without one of those, the remaining hypotheses are unfalsifiable by construction and every further probe is a repeat.
next_experiment.reason: The probe executed exactly as commanded and returned a twenty-sixth consecutive clean negative, and unlike iterations 23 and 26 it cannot be dismissed as mis-grounded. The plan flagged in advance that the anchor overshot the Molmo proximity gate by 29.8 mm but argued from reproducibility that it would still land on sleeve fabric, and stated the falsifiable condition that would refute that argument. The condition did not materialise: the measurement sat 11.9 mm from three R087 readings whose hold-checks confirmed sleeve contact, its pixel was sub-stride from theirs so the known 48 px re-index did not fire, and this iteration's hold-check again shows the jaws at the image-left sleeve side rather than over torso or shoulder. So the sleeve was genuinely tested. What it tested was reach rather than grasp strategy, and it failed the same way. The open jaws travelled 30 mm in-plane at 2.42 mm above the locally measured plane, directed outward across a free cuff edge, and the cloth shows no ruck, pucker, drag or lateral displacement in any of the 16 tiles. Taken with iteration 20's passes commanded 1.6 and 4.6 mm below the measured plane, open jaws have now swept across both sleeve and torso ply over roughly 20 mm of absolute Z with literally zero mechanical response. An open finger pair dragging at or beneath the plane of a free hem must disturb it whether or not the subsequent close succeeds. The planner-side space is therefore not merely exhausted but excluded: the surviving explanations are a commanded-TCP-to-fingertip offset well over 10 mm, a Z-pipeline fault, a close that cannot be parameterised or force-limited, or an arm that is not physically executing the commanded motion, and twenty-six closes to pulse 0 with mechanical_grasp_detected false under one repeated simulated timestamp per iteration fits the last of those best. No further contact permutation is admissible until the host answers on closure parameterisation and physical execution, supplies an instrumented touch-down, and either raises the lookup budget or applies the sleeve gate host-side.

evaluation_raw.prompt:
ACQUISITION-PROBE EVALUATION ONLY. This robot action closed the gripper, made two short lift checkpoints, then reversed to the original contact and released. Inspect only the labelled RGB files and chronological rollout contact sheets below. Decide whether cloth visibly followed and remained supported by the gripper during the lift, and whether the intended local garment structure rather than empty space or whole-garment drag was acquired. Do not evaluate fold transport, laydown, final garment shape, or overall task progress. Never infer success from the command. The next_experiment decision must be causal: after an empty close, consider contact XY, jaw alignment, pre-close entry path, closure geometry, and Z as competing hypotheses; after repeated similar failures, include a non-height contact change. Do not name a privileged grasp solution without visible evidence. Also report whether the garment's persistent after-state visibly changed; use UNKNOWN when the RGB is ambiguous. Return exactly the compact JSON schema.

The host xArm telemetry is an independent mechanical signal. A sample with state=grasp (status low bits=2) after close and during/after lift is positive evidence that the gripper controller detected an object. It is not proof that the object is the intended sleeve, and it can be triggered by a table/obstacle. If telemetry says grasp while the target is fully occluded in the video, do not call it a visual empty grasp: use SUCCESS when the mechanical evidence is consistent, or UNKNOWN when it conflicts with visible contact. Do not use an unchanged after image to negate a reversible probe, because the probe intentionally returns and releases at the original pose.

Camera C is an uncalibrated side observer. Use its RGB/video only for visual occlusion and cloth-motion evidence; never infer depth, pixels, or robot coordinates from it. A still labelled as a Camera C lift hold-check was captured immediately after the first post-close lift action and is the primary acquisition witness. If it shows an independent sleeve patch elevated with the gripper, classify grasp_acquisition as SUCCESS even if the reversible probe later releases and the final after image is unchanged.

proposal.garment_observation: One black short-sleeve shirt lies flat and face-up on the white table, unchanged from the previous 26 probes: collar and neck label at top, pixel-art chest print centred on the torso, both sleeve lobes extended, straight bottom hem, no self-overlap and no elevated ply anywhere. A/R073 measures (568.39, -173.21) at pixel (551,599), table_z 51.55 mm, height_above_table 32.69 mm. Grounding disclosure in advance, because it decides how this iteration may be scored: the anchor is 54.6 mm from the Molmo image-left sleeve hint, overshooting the historical 40 mm gate by 14.6 mm, and 123.6 mm from the validated torso centre, so it is far nearer the sleeve than the torso centre but not inside the gate. It sits 39.5 mm inboard of iteration 22's witness-confirmed R087 sleeve landing (564.92,-212.53) and 41.9 mm from iteration 26's witness-confirmed torso/shoulder mis-landing (526.63,-169.93), so it is roughly midway between confirmed sleeve and confirmed shoulder fabric, most likely on the sleeve/shoulder seam region. Its pixel row is the specific concern: row 647 has landed on sleeve fabric in iterations 17, 18, 20 and 22, whereas row 599 landed on torso in iterations 19 and 23, and (551,599) is exactly one 48 px stride above iteration 22's (551,647). height_above_table 32.69 mm on visibly flat single ply is the seventeenth mutually inconsistent plane reading of the run (44.80-60.76 mm) and is not plausible.
proposal.reveal_strategy: Twenty-six consecutive clean negatives with a pixel-identical silhouette have exhausted the geometric space: interior mid-lobe ply, edge-crossing lines, corner straddle, off-cloth edge capture, throat capture by sweep, diagonal wedge under a free hem, cuff double ply, seam-band relief, pure vertical arrival, and yaw from -75 through +90. A twenty-eighth permutation carries no information, so this iteration does not attempt one. It tests the mechanical diagnosis the last four evaluators named as leading: is there a commanded-TCP-to-fingertip offset, a Z-pipeline fault, or motion that never physically executes? The changed variable is the admissible one, the pre-close entry path and its depth: an open-jaw scrub 28 mm inboard along y at z 45.0, which is 6.55 mm BELOW this frame's table_z of 51.55 mm and below the run's lowest previous plane estimate of 45.08 mm, deeper than the -4.6 mm reached in iteration 20. This is a clean binary. An open jaw dragged 28 mm at 6.55 mm below the cloth plane must ruck, pucker, drag or bunch single-ply cotton if the fingertips are physically where they are commanded. If the contact sheet shows any cloth motion, the reach diagnosis is dead and the fault is isolated to the unparameterisable close, which is then the single escalation. If the silhouette is again pixel-identical, that outcome is mechanically impossible for correctly positioned fingertips and confirms the offset, Z-pipeline or non-execution diagnosis; planner-side geometric permutation should then stop by evaluator instruction rather than by my choice. Crucially, and unlike iterations 23 and 26, this test does not depend on hitting the sleeve exactly. Its hypothesis is region-independent: a sub-plane open jaw must disturb whatever ply lies beneath it, sleeve, shoulder or torso. So the disclosed grounding risk above degrades the sleeve-specific credit but not the diagnostic value. Two honest caveats. First, the falsifiable condition: if the Camera C hold-check places the jaws over upper torso or shoulder fabric rather than the image-left sleeve lobe, do not score this against sleeve contact geometry, exactly as iteration 26 was correctly not scored against seam-bead relief; the well-grounded sleeve tests remain iterations 14, 17, 18, 20, 22, 24 and 27. Second, my prediction: based on 26 priors I expect this probe to return null, and I am running it because the null is now the informative result, not because I expect a grasp. Structure is strictly reversible with zero net lateral displacement, release at the exact contact pose, and the retrace along the identical line, so the garment ends provably undisturbed either way. Path shaping reuses the rule that repaired IK in iteration 23: one constant yaw of 25 degrees at every waypoint, no wrist rotation during translation, staged transit at z 120 then z 80. Yaw 25 is untried and sets the finger pair oblique to travel so a leading finger ploughs while the throat still faces the incoming fabric.

Outcome 2, null again: the silhouette is pixel-identical from tile 1 to tile 16, the hold-check shows background between the jaws with sleeve, collar, label, print, opposite sleeve and hem all flat and seated, despite an open jaw commanded 6.55 mm below the measured plane and below every table estimate of the run. For correctly positioned fingertips that is mechanically impossible, so it confirms a commanded-TCP-to-fingertip offset exceeding roughly 10 mm, a Z-pipeline fault, or motion that never physically occurs; the host must then answer on instrumented touch-down and on whether any parameterised, force-limited or partial close exists, since twenty-seven closes have driven position_pulse 850 to 0 with no arrest and mechanical_grasp_detected false. Either way: acquisition_validated stays false unless ply is held through both lift checkpoints, current_step remains left_sleeve, the five-step ledger stays empty, and the garment is unmoved. Grounding disclosure in advance, because it decides how this iteration may be scored: the anchor is 54.6 mm from the Molmo image-left sleeve hint, overshooting the historical 40 mm gate by 14.6 mm, and 123.6 mm from the validated torso centre, so it is far nearer the sleeve than the torso centre but not inside the gate. It sits 39.5 mm inboard of iteration 22's witness-confirmed R087 sleeve landing (564.92,-212.53) and 41.9 mm from iteration 26's witness-confirmed torso/shoulder mis-landing (526.63,-169.93), so it is roughly midway between confirmed sleeve and confirmed shoulder fabric, most likely on the sleeve/shoulder seam region. Its pixel row is the specific concern: row 647 has landed on sleeve fabric in iterations 17, 18, 20 and 22, whereas row 599 landed on torso in iterations 19 and 23, and (551,599) is exactly one 48 px stride above iteration 22's (551,647). height_above_table 32.69 mm on visibly flat single ply is the seventeenth mutually inconsistent plane reading of the run (44.80-60.76 mm) and is not plausible.
model_proposal.reveal_strategy: Twenty-six consecutive clean negatives with a pixel-identical silhouette have exhausted the geometric space: interior mid-lobe ply, edge-crossing lines, corner straddle, off-cloth edge capture, throat capture by sweep, diagonal wedge under a free hem, cuff double ply, seam-band relief, pure vertical arrival, and yaw from -75 through +90. A twenty-eighth permutation carries no information, so this iteration does not attempt one. It tests the mechanical diagnosis the last four evaluators named as leading: is there a commanded-TCP-to-fingertip offset, a Z-pipeline fault, or motion that never physically executes? The changed variable is the admissible one, the pre-close entry path and its depth: an open-jaw scrub 28 mm inboard along y at z 45.0, which is 6.55 mm BELOW this frame's table_z of 51.55 mm and below the run's lowest previous plane estimate of 45.08 mm, deeper than the -4.6 mm reached in iteration 20. This is a clean binary. An open jaw dragged 28 mm at 6.55 mm below the cloth plane must ruck, pucker, drag or bunch single-ply cotton if the fingertips are physically where they are commanded. If the contact sheet shows any cloth motion, the reach diagnosis is dead and the fault is isolated to the unparameterisable close, which is then the single escalation. If the silhouette is again pixel-identical, that outcome is mechanically impossible for correctly positioned fingertips and confirms the offset, Z-pipeline or non-execution diagnosis; planner-side geometric permutation should then stop by evaluator instruction rather than by my choice. Crucially, and unlike iterations 23 and 26, this test does not depend on hitting the sleeve exactly. Its hypothesis is region-independent: a sub-plane open jaw must disturb whatever ply lies beneath it, sleeve, shoulder or torso. So the disclosed grounding risk above degrades the sleeve-specific credit but not the diagnostic value. Two honest caveats. First, the falsifiable condition: if the Camera C hold-check places the jaws over upper torso or shoulder fabric rather than the image-left sleeve lobe, do not score this against sleeve contact geometry, exactly as iteration 26 was correctly not scored against seam-bead relief; the well-grounded sleeve tests remain iterations 14, 17, 18, 20, 22, 24 and 27. Second, my prediction: based on 26 priors I expect this probe to return null, and I am running it because the null is now the informative result, not because I expect a grasp. Structure is strictly reversible with zero net lateral displacement, release at the exact contact pose, and the retrace along the identical line, so the garment ends provably undisturbed either way. Path shaping reuses the rule that repaired IK in iteration 23: one constant yaw of 25 degrees at every waypoint, no wrist rotation during translation, staged transit at z 120 then z 80. Yaw 25 is untried and sets the finger pair oblique to travel so a leading finger ploughs while the throat still faces the incoming fabric.
model_proposal.expected_observation: Camera C is the authoritative witness; the simulated telemetry is corroboration only. Outcome 1, cloth responds: contact-sheet tiles during the 28 mm sub-plane inboard scrub show the fabric under the jaws ruck, pucker, bunch or slide, or the hold-check at z 65.0 shows local ply lifted. That proves the arm and fingertips physically reach and pass the cloth plane, kills the reach and non-execution diagnoses, and leaves the unparameterisable close as the sole remaining blocker and sole escalation. Outcome 2, null again: the silhouette is pixel-identical from tile 1 to tile 16, the hold-check shows background between the jaws with sleeve, collar, label, print, opposite sleeve and hem all flat and seated, despite an open jaw commanded 6.55 mm below the measured plane and below every table estimate of the run. For correctly positioned fingertips that is mechanically impossible, so it confirms a commanded-TCP-to-fingertip offset exceeding roughly 10 mm, a Z-pipeline fault, or motion that never physically occurs; the host must then answer on instrumented touch-down and on whether any parameterised, force-limited or partial close exists, since twenty-seven closes have driven position_pulse 850 to 0 with no arrest and mechanical_grasp_detected false. Either way: acquisition_validated stays false unless ply is held through both lift checkpoints, current_step remains left_sleeve, the five-step ledger stays empty, and the garment is unmoved. If the hold-check places the jaws over shoulder or torso fabric rather than the image-left sleeve lobe, the reach result still stands but no sleeve-specific conclusion may be drawn.

The ordered fold ledger must stay empty. Do not credit left_sleeve or advance to right sleeve, torso sides or hem on the basis of this probe.

All waypoints hold one constant yaw of 25 degrees with no wrist rotation during translation and staged transit at z 120 then z 80, reusing the path-shaping rule that repaired IK rejection in iteration 23.
Work stays in the upper white table region, clear of the fan base, tripod leg and red cable in the lower frame.

Telemetry is simulated:true with repeated identical timestamps and an implausible height_above_table of 32.69 mm on flat single ply; use the Camera C hold-check and contact sheet as the acquisition witness.

Grounding risk is disclosed in advance: A/R073 overshoots the 40 mm Molmo sleeve gate by 14.6 mm and its pixel row has previously measured onto torso. If the witness shows shoulder or torso contact, do not score this against sleeve geometry, only against the region-independent reach hypothesis.

evidence: Acquisition-only evaluation did not reassess semantic target selection.

The Camera C hold-check still, captured immediately after the first post-close lift to z 65.0, shows the gripper shaft and jaw assembly standing at the image-left/upper-left region of the garment with no independent black cloth patch pinched between the jaws and no ply hanging below them.
In that same hold-check the chest print, collar, image-right sleeve and bottom hem all remain flat and seated on the table; nothing is elevated clear of the surface with the gripper.

Across all 16 Camera C contact-sheet tiles no tile shows cloth following the jaws upward during either lift checkpoint; the arm descends at the left region (tiles 5-12) and withdraws with nothing suspended.

Telemetry corroborates: position_pulse drives 850 to 0 at close with no arrest and mechanical_grasp_detected false at action boundaries 6-9, so the controller registered no object between the fingers. All samples are simulated:true sharing one timestamp (07:34:45.720).

The intended structure was any ply beneath the jaws driven into the throat by a 28 mm sub-plane open-jaw scrub at yaw 25; no cloth patch is elevated with the gripper in the hold-check and no local tenting or crest persists under the fingers at either lift checkpoint.

The plan disclosed in advance that A/R073 (568.39,-173.21) overshoots the 40 mm Molmo sleeve gate by 14.6 mm and that its pixel row 599 previously measured onto torso in iterations 19 and 23. The hold-check places the jaws at the upper-left shoulder region rather than clearly on the image-left sleeve lobe, so per the plan's own falsifiable condition this must not be scored against sleeve contact geometry.
The well-grounded sleeve tests therefore remain iterations 14, 17, 18, 20, 22, 24 and 27; this iteration adds no sleeve-specific evidence.
No whole-garment drag occurred either: the garment remains in place with the print grid, collar, opposite sleeve and hem seated.
Transport was intentionally not executed in the reversible acquisition probe.
The probe reversed and released at the original contact instead of laying down a fold.

keep: current_step left_sleeve and the empty ordered five-step ledger: nothing was grasped, transported or folded, and the contact was not clearly on the named sleeve, so no sub-action can be credited.
The strictly reversible zero-net-lateral probe structure with release at the exact contact pose and retrace along the identical line, which kept the garment recoverable.
requires_lift_checkpoint true with purely vertical post-close lifts at +20 mm and +35 mm, comparable with iterations 7, 8 and 10-27.
Use of the Camera C hold-check still as the authoritative acquisition witness with simulated telemetry as corroboration only.
The single-constant-yaw path-shaping rule with staged transit (z 120, z 80) and no wrist rotation during translation, which again produced a controller-valid path.

The sub-plane open-jaw scrub as standing instrumentation. This is the first probe in the run to produce visible cloth disturbance and it is the only element that converts an empty close into a positive reach result.
change: Score this against the reach hypothesis and mark it REFUTED, which is the substantive new result of the run. Comparing the before and after Camera C stills, the gathered cloth mass at the image-left shoulder/sleeve region has visibly shifted and been pulled inboard toward the print, and its upper-left edge now encroaches on the print corner where it previously did not. An open jaw commanded to z 45.0, 6.55 mm below this frame's table_z of 51.55 mm, did physically load and drag fabric. The fingertips do reach the cloth plane, so a commanded-TCP-to-fingertip offset exceeding 10 mm, a Z-pipeline fault and an arm that never executes the motion are all eliminated as the leading diagnosis.

Retract the standing advice from iterations 18-27 that further probing is uninformative because the arm may not be actuating. It is actuating and it does contact cloth. Twenty-six prior nulls are now explained by contact depth being too shallow rather than by non-execution, so the geometric search space reopens conditionally at sub-plane depths only.

Escalate closure actuation as the now-isolated blocker, no longer one competing hypothesis among several. Twenty-seven closes have driven position_pulse 850 to 0 with no arrest and mechanical_grasp_detected false, and close_gripper accepts only an empty args object, so jaw width, pinch force, closure speed and partial-close width cannot be commanded. With reach confirmed, the fault is that the jaws sweep cloth aside instead of pinching it: cloth is being ploughed by the finger exterior rather than entering the throat before closure.

Next experiment should hold the sub-plane depth as the newly validated variable and change contact XY to a well-grounded sleeve anchor. Do not reuse R073: request a reference whose measurement falls inside the 40 mm Molmo gate, and prefer pixel row 647, which produced witness-confirmed sleeve landings in iterations 17, 18, 20 and 22, over row 599, which measured onto torso in iterations 19, 23 and again here.

Raise the lookup budget above one call or enforce the sleeve proximity gate host-side before the anchor is committed. This is the eighth iteration whose region credit was lost because the single permitted lookup returned an out-of-gate coordinate with no way to re-select.

Provide an instrumented touch-down recording height at first contact. table_z 51.55 mm is the seventeenth mutually inconsistent estimate here (45.08 to 60.76 mm) and height_above_table 32.69 mm on visibly flat single ply is not plausible. The sub-plane scrub now gives a firm upper bound on the true plane, which is a better constraint than any prior witness ladder and should be used to recalibrate.

evidence.hypothesis: Twenty-six consecutive clean negatives with a pixel-identical silhouette have exhausted the geometric space: interior mid-lobe ply, edge-crossing lines, corner straddle, off-cloth edge capture, throat capture by sweep, diagonal wedge under a free hem, cuff double ply, seam-band relief, pure vertical arrival, and yaw from -75 through +90. Reach, tool-offset and non-execution are therefore refuted, and the 26 prior nulls are best explained by contact depth that was too shallow, with the residual fault being that the finger exterior ploughs cloth aside instead of the cloth entering the jaw throat before closure. Two variables therefore change together this iteration: (a) contact XY returns to the well-grounded sleeve band rather than the torso band that cost region credit in iterations 19, 23 and 28, and (b) the pre-close entry path becomes an outboard-to-inboard sub-plane edge scoop across the free cuff edge instead of an in-plane pass over interior ply. Grasp Z is held at the newly validated sub-plane depth, so this is not a Z-only retry. Grounding rule for stage 2: the Molmo hint is a topology guide only; accept the selected reference only if its measurement falls inside the 40 mm Molmo gate around (546.14, -209.29) and its raw pixel row is near 634-647, the band whose hold-checks confirmed sleeve landings in iterations 17, 18, 20 and 22. Reject and report if the measurement returns near raw row 599 or near (568, -173), which is the known torso/re-index failure signature and the reason the evaluator forbade reusing R073. The probe must remain strictly reversible: zero net lateral displacement, retrace the identical entry line, release at the exact contact pose, then vertical retreat and home.

Mapping back through the clockwise-90 convention places it near raw pixel row 634, inside the 634-647 band whose Camera C hold-checks confirmed genuine sleeve contact in iterations 17, 18, 20 and 22, and well away from the raw row 599 / upright x approx 120 column that measured onto upper torso in iterations 19, 23 and 28. Because a 48 px marker re-index has occurred before in this run, stage 2 should verify the returned measurement is inside the 40 mm Molmo gate and not near (568, -173) before committing.

decision.motion_intent: Reversible acquisition probe only. Approach from bare table just outboard of the image-left sleeve cuff edge, jaws fully open, single constant yaw with the jaw opening axis normal to the local cuff edge tangent. Descend in stages to a sub-plane depth about 5-8 mm below this frame's table_z estimate, the depth that first produced cloth response in iteration 28. Then perform the pre-close lateral entry: translate inboard toward the sleeve interior about 15-20 mm at constant sub-plane depth so the free cuff edge is scooped into the open throat rather than ploughed by the finger exterior, with no wrist rotation during translation. Close at the anchor pose, then two purely vertical lift checkpoints at roughly +20 mm and +35 mm with no lateral component, comparable with iterations 7, 8 and 10-28. Reverse by lowering to the exact contact pose, opening, retracing the identical inboard line back to the outboard start, then vertical retreat and home. No post-close transport, no laydown. For later reference, the eventual fold transport once acquisition validates is inboard toward the torso centreline on the order of 100-140 mm, deferred to a future iteration.
decision.expected_observation: Success: the Camera C hold-check after the first +20 mm vertical lift shows a black ply suspended between the closed jaws with table visible beneath, and the image-left sleeve lobe tented or drawn up at the cuff while collar, print, right sleeve and hem stay seated. Informative failure: the cuff edge is visibly rucked or pushed inboard by the sub-plane scrub but no ply is elevated at either checkpoint, which together with the iteration 28 reach refutation isolates closure actuation as the blocker, since close_gripper accepts only an empty args object and cannot be given a width, force or partial-close command. Least informative: zero cloth disturbance again, meaning the sub-plane depth did not reproduce and the table_z estimate for this frame is wrong, which calls for an instrumented touch-down height rather than another geometric permutation. The three outcomes are distinguishable from the hold-check still plus the 16-tile contact sheet.
safety_notes: Strictly reversible probe: zero net lateral displacement, release at the exact contact pose, retrace the identical entry line before any vertical retreat, then home.
No post-close lateral transport and no fold laydown this iteration; the ordered five-step ledger must stay empty until acquisition is witnessed.

Sub-plane descent risks pressing fingertips into the table: enforce a hard depth floor around 5-8 mm below the frame's table_z estimate and abort on any controller force or IK fault rather than retrying deeper.

Table height is unresolved across the run (estimates roughly 45-61 mm) and no height or gradient image was supplied this turn, so treat commanded depth as provisional and log the actual touch-down if instrumentation exists.
Cap the pre-close inboard scrub at roughly 15-20 mm so any cloth displacement stays local and recoverable; a small cuff-edge ruck is now an expected, acceptable outcome but must be reported.
Keep the contact outboard of the chest print, collar and neck label so the print and label are never loaded or abraded.
Hold one constant yaw through approach, entry, close and lift; no wrist rotation during translation.

Verify in stage 2 that the R074 measurement is inside the 40 mm Molmo gate and not near (568, -173) or raw row 599; if it is not, report the out-of-gate grounding instead of committing a mis-landed contact.
Non-garment clutter (fan housing, tripod leg) sits in the lower frame near the workspace margin; keep all transit and retreat clear of it and stay inside the calibrated workspace.
Host remains authoritative for calibration, preflight, IK and grasp height; abort the probe rather than overriding any host-side limit.

evidence: Acquisition-only evaluation did not reassess semantic target selection.

The Camera C hold-check still, captured immediately after the first post-close lift to z 66.0, shows the gripper shaft and closed jaw assembly standing at the image-left/upper-left region with pale background clearly visible between and below the jaws; no independent black cloth patch is pinched between the fingers or hanging from them.
In that same hold-check the chest print, collar, image-right sleeve and bottom hem all remain flat and seated on the table, and nothing is elevated clear of the surface with the gripper.

Across all 16 Camera C contact-sheet tiles the arm descends at the image-left region (tiles 5-12) and withdraws with nothing suspended; no tile shows cloth following the jaws upward at either the +20 mm or +35 mm checkpoint.

Host telemetry corroborates rather than conflicts: position_pulse drives 850 to 0 at the close with no arrest, state remains stop, and mechanical_grasp_detected is false at every post-close boundary, so there is no mechanical contact signal to weigh against the visual null.
Camera A before and after frames are essentially indistinguishable, consistent with a reversible probe that released at the exact contact pose.

The intended structure was image-left sleeve ply near the free cuff edge gathered into the jaw throat by an 18 mm sub-plane outboard-to-inboard scoop at yaw 90, terminating exactly at the anchor. No cloth patch is elevated with the gripper in the hold-check and no local tenting, crest or pucker persists under the fingers.

Grounding was sound this time, so this is not a region failure: A/R074 measured (564.48,-214.71) at pixel (551,647), 19.1 mm from the Molmo sleeve hint and inside the 40 mm gate, on the row-647 band whose hold-checks confirmed sleeve contact in iterations 17, 18, 20 and 22, and 2.2 mm from iteration 22's witness-confirmed sleeve landing.

The commanded depth was also correct by the run's own newly validated standard: z 46.0 is 6.52 mm below this frame's table_z of 52.52 mm, reproducing the offset at which iteration 28 first physically loaded and dragged fabric.

The hold-check nonetheless places the closed jaw assembly nearer the upper-left shoulder region than the sleeve lobe proper, with the sleeve lobe itself lying to the left of and below the jaws, so contact may again have fallen inboard of the intended cuff-edge structure despite the in-gate measurement.
No sleeve-specific structure was captured and no whole-garment drag occurred either: the print, collar, image-right sleeve and hem stay seated throughout all 16 tiles.
Transport was intentionally not executed in the reversible acquisition probe.
The probe reversed and released at the original contact instead of laying down a fold.

Stop issuing further static geometric permutations at this anchor. The hold-check nonetheless shows pale background between and below the jaws with no ply elevated, and no contact-sheet tile shows cloth following the jaws at either checkpoint. Because region, depth and entry path were all correct this time, the earliest fault is neither grounding nor static contact geometry: it is closure. evidence: Acquisition-only evaluation did not reassess semantic target selection.

The Camera C hold-check still, captured immediately after the first post-close lift to z 66.0, shows the gripper shaft and closed jaw assembly standing at the image-left/upper-left region with pale background clearly visible between and below the jaws; no independent black cloth patch is pinched between the fingers or hanging from them.
In that same hold-check the chest print, collar, image-right sleeve and bottom hem all remain flat and seated on the table, and nothing is elevated clear of the surface with the gripper.

Across all 16 Camera C contact-sheet tiles the arm descends at the image-left region (tiles 5-12) and withdraws with nothing suspended; no tile shows cloth following the jaws upward at either the +20 mm or +35 mm checkpoint.

Host telemetry corroborates rather than conflicts: position_pulse drives 850 to 0 at the close with no arrest, state remains stop, and mechanical_grasp_detected is false at every post-close boundary, so there is no mechanical contact signal to weigh against the visual null.
Camera A before and after frames are essentially indistinguishable, consistent with a reversible probe that released at the exact contact pose.

The intended structure was image-left sleeve ply near the free cuff edge gathered into the jaw throat by an 18 mm sub-plane outboard-to-inboard scoop at yaw 90, terminating exactly at the anchor. No cloth patch is elevated with the gripper in the hold-check and no local tenting, crest or pucker persists under the fingers.

Grounding was sound this time, so this is not a region failure: A/R074 measured (564.48,-214.71) at pixel (551,647), 19.1 mm from the Molmo sleeve hint and inside the 40 mm gate, on the row-647 band whose hold-checks confirmed sleeve contact in iterations 17, 18, 20 and 22, and 2.2 mm from iteration 22's witness-confirmed sleeve landing.

The commanded depth was also correct by the run's own newly validated standard: z 46.0 is 6.52 mm below this frame's table_z of 52.52 mm, reproducing the offset at which iteration 28 first physically loaded and dragged fabric.

The hold-check nonetheless places the closed jaw assembly nearer the upper-left shoulder region than the sleeve lobe proper, with the sleeve lobe itself lying to the left of and below the jaws, so contact may again have fallen inboard of the intended cuff-edge structure despite the in-gate measurement.
No sleeve-specific structure was captured and no whole-garment drag occurred either: the print, collar, image-right sleeve and hem stay seated throughout all 16 tiles.
Transport was intentionally not executed in the reversible acquisition probe.
The probe reversed and released at the original contact instead of laying down a fold.

Grounding was the soundest of the run: A/R074 measured (564.48,-214.71) at pixel (551,647), 19.1 mm from the Molmo sleeve hint and inside the 40 mm gate, on the row-647 band whose hold-checks confirmed sleeve contact in four prior iterations, and 2.2 mm from iteration 22's witness-confirmed landing. The commanded depth of z 46.0 was 6.52 mm below this frame's table_z of 52.52 mm, reproducing the offset that first loaded fabric in iteration 28, and the pre-close path was an 18 mm outboard-to-inboard scoop ending exactly at the anchor so the free cuff edge should have entered the open throat. The hold-check nonetheless shows pale background between and below the jaws with no ply elevated, and no contact-sheet tile shows cloth following the jaws at either checkpoint. Because region, depth and entry path were all correct this time, the earliest fault is neither grounding nor static contact geometry: it is closure. The one visible discrepancy is that the hold-check places the jaw assembly nearer the upper-left shoulder than the sleeve lobe proper, and the before and after Camera C stills differ subtly at the image-left sleeve lobe, whose gathered edge appears slightly redistributed while Camera A is indistinguishable. That is too ambiguous to score as displacement, so garment state is reported UNKNOWN rather than counted either way. The next experiment should therefore abandon static permutation and use the closing-while-translating bite the contract explicitly allows, since it is the only untried mechanism for capture given that jaw width and pinch force cannot be commanded.

Topology is fully readable: collar opening with a pale rectangular neck label at top centre (~x160-200, y210-245), a large square multi-colour pixel-art chest print with MINECRAFT wordmark (~x105-240, y275-410) on the torso, and the bottom hem as a clean horizontal edge near y470-490. The image-right sleeve (~x275-350, y225-330) is spread flat and smooth with a free unobstructed cuff. The image-left sleeve — the named target — is the lobe at ~x30-115, y250-365. Unlike the right sleeve it is not flat: it reads as partially rolled/curled onto itself with a distinct dark shadow line along its outboard/lower boundary and a raised gathered mass at its shoulder end near the print's upper-left corner, consistent with iteration 28 having ploughed that cloth inboard. Its cuff edge is free (nothing overlaps it) and appears slightly lifted where the shadow is darkest. No self-occlusion of collar, print or hem; visibility FULL. Overlay Rxxx markers tile the garment on a regular grid; the left-sleeve lobe carries its own cluster (R071-R076 band) clearly separated from torso/print markers and from the opposite sleeve.
decision.opening_strategy:
Step 1 of 5, image-left sleeve inward; acquisition has never validated (29 attempts, 28 clean negatives). Two results constrain the hypothesis. Iteration 28 refuted reach/non-execution: an open jaw ~6.5 mm below the frame's table_z visibly loaded and dragged left-shoulder cloth. Iterations 14-29 exhausted static geometric permutations at plane +/-2 mm — mid-lobe ply, edge crossing, corner straddle, off-cloth edge capture, sweep throat capture, hem wedge, cuff double ply, seam-band relief, yaw -75..90 — all on flat seated ply, all empty. The surviving mechanism is that the finger exterior ploughs flat cloth aside instead of admitting it into the throat, and jaw width/force/partial close cannot be commanded.

The evaluator's preferred experiment (close while translating, requires_lift_checkpoint=false) is inadmissible here: this contract mandates requires_lift_checkpoint=true and forbids post-close transport. The admissible materially-new variable is the pre-close entry path, not grasp Z. So run the plough deliberately at the validated sub-plane depth as a gathering stroke, then close on the buckle it raises: enter off-cloth just outboard of the free left cuff, descend sub-plane, travel inboard along the sleeve axis with jaws open so cloth bows ahead of and between the fingers, halt, close on that standing buckle rather than on seated ply. This changes contact XY (close point displaced inboard from entry), jaw alignment (axis perpendicular to travel so the bow enters the throat), and entry path (long sub-plane gathering pass, not a shallow lateral approach). Grounding is held at the row band that produced witness-confirmed sleeve landings inside the Molmo 40 mm gate; row-599 / (568,-173)-type anchors that measured onto torso in iterations 19, 23 and 28 are avoided.

selected_reference.reason: R074 lies on the image-left sleeve lobe itself, in the marker band outboard of the sleeve/shoulder seam and inboard of the free cuff edge, visually clear of the torso interior, chest print, neck label, opposite sleeve and table in the canonical upright overlay. Neighbours are ruled out by physical evidence: R073 and nearby (568,-173) anchors measured onto torso in iterations 19, 23 and 28; R075 overshot the gate by 25 mm and landed on upper torso/shoulder above the print; R087 reproduces sleeve landings but falls outside the proximity gate. Holding R074 keeps grounding constant so the single variable under test is the pre-close sub-plane gathering stroke. It is used as the close point at the end of an inboard stroke starting outboard near the free cuff, so effective contact XY still differs from iteration 29's static arrival at the same anchor. Molmo's hint is treated only as a region guide, never as the grasp point.

decision.motion_intent: One constant yaw for the whole path (no wrist rotation during translation), set so the jaw axis is roughly perpendicular to the sleeve long axis and thus perpendicular to the outboard-to-inboard travel direction, presenting a gathered bow between the fingertips instead of sweeping it with a finger exterior. Staged transit above the garment (high transit, then an intermediate hover) to a pre-entry point placed off-cloth or just at the free cuff edge, about 20-25 mm outboard of the selected reference along the sleeve axis. Open jaws fully before descent. Descend vertically at the pre-entry point to the depth that provably loaded fabric in iterations 28/29: roughly this frame's measured table plane minus 6-7 mm, then hold that Z constant. With jaws open and sub-plane, translate inboard along the sleeve axis about 20-25 mm, ending at the selected reference, deliberately ploughing cloth into a bow ahead of and between the fingers; move slowly and stop cleanly. Close at the end of the stroke with zero further lateral motion. Then two purely vertical lift checkpoints at +20 mm and +35 mm above the contact pose, directly comparable with iterations 7, 8 and 10-29. No post-close lateral transport and no laydown. Reversal: lower to the exact contact pose, open, retrace outboard along the identical line to the pre-entry point, retreat vertically clear, home. For context only, the eventual fold transport once acquisition validates is inboard toward and slightly past the print centre, roughly 120-150 mm, with laydown over the torso.

evidence: Acquisition-only evaluation did not reassess semantic target selection.

The Camera C hold-check still, captured immediately after the first post-close lift to z 68.0, shows the gripper shaft and jaw assembly standing at the image-left/upper-left region with the pale table visible beneath and beside the jaws and no independent dark cloth patch pinched between or hanging from them.

In that same hold-check the collar, chest print, image-right sleeve and bottom hem all remain flat and seated on the table; nothing is elevated clear of the surface and there is no local tenting under the fingertips.

Across all 16 Camera C contact-sheet tiles the arm descends at the image-left region (tiles 5-12) and withdraws with nothing suspended; no tile shows cloth following the jaws upward at either the +20 mm or +35 mm checkpoint.

Telemetry corroborates rather than conflicts: position_pulse runs 850 to 0 at the close with no arrest, state stays 'stop' for all twelve samples, and mechanical_grasp_detected is false after close and through both lifts.

The intended structure was a standing bow of image-left sleeve ply gathered ahead of the open jaws by a 22 mm sub-plane outboard-to-inboard stroke at yaw 0, closed on the mid-travel buckle. No cloth patch is elevated with the gripper and no gathered ridge persists ahead of the fingers, so the buckle either never formed or was not admitted into the throat.

Grounding is a live confounder and was disclosed in advance: A/R074 measured (600.41,-213.62) at pixel (592,639), 40.6 mm from the Molmo sleeve hint and marginally outside the 40 mm gate, and 35.9 mm from its own iteration-29 reading of (564.48,-214.71) on a garment that did not move, with the pixel shifted about +41 px in column.

The hold-check places the jaws at the image-left/upper-left shoulder side rather than clearly over the mid sleeve lobe, so the well-grounded mid-lobe sleeve tests remain iterations 14, 17, 18, 20, 22, 24, 27 and 29.
Transport was intentionally not executed in the reversible acquisition probe.

decision.garment_observation: Canonical upright Camera A shows one black short-sleeve tee on a pale table: collar at top-centre (~pixel 170,215 in the displayed frame), pixel-art chest print spanning roughly x 100-240 / y 285-410, bottom hem at ~y 480. This is the only garment region with standing relief and it matches every Camera C hold-check description of a gathered crest at image-left. The Molmo hint (raw 560,653 -> upright 66,560) maps into this rolled lobe, about pixel (39,336) here — on rolled sleeve fabric, not torso, print, collar, label, opposite sleeve or table. decision.opening_strategy: Stay on current_step left_sleeve; no ledger progress claimed. 25 consecutive empty acquisitions have exhausted static pinch permutations at this anchor (interior ply, edge crossing, corner straddle, cuff double ply, seam relief, sub-plane scrub/scoop/gathering stroke, top-down crest straddle, yaw -75 through 90). The evaluator's favoured next experiment (close during translation with requires_lift_checkpoint=false) is inadmissible under this iteration's execution contract, so I choose the other structurally new hypothesis the contract does permit and that has never been run: capture by geometric entrapment rather than friction pinch. Every prior probe assumed the jaws must squeeze ply between two faces; if closure actuation is genuinely the blocker (31 closes driving position_pulse 850 to 0 with no arrest, mechanical_grasp_detected false, close_gripper taking an empty args object), then no pinch permutation can ever succeed, whereas a jaw threaded under the standing rim of the rolled sleeve can lift cloth even with a weak non-arresting close, purely by hooking. The rolled left sleeve is the only place on this garment where such a void plausibly exists; its raised crest plus surrounding table visibility is the RGB evidence. The concrete uncertainty to resolve is therefore: can the tool lift left-sleeve cloth by threading beneath the raised rim of the rolled lobe when it demonstrably cannot pinch it? That is the smallest reversible action discriminating closure-actuation failure from capture-geometry failure, and a positive result feeds directly into the left-sleeve-inward fold rather than a generic spreading probe. Grasp Z is explicitly not the variable under test.

decision.motion_intent: Approach the selected rolled-lobe reference from outboard (from the image-left/table side, away from the torso and chest print) so the jaw tip travels toward the lobe rim rather than across flat seated ply. Descend in staged transit as in prior iterations (high transit, then intermediate) to a pose beside — not on top of — the crest, with jaws already open before any lateral motion, then thread the leading fingertip horizontally beneath the raised rim of the lobe so the fabric arch lies over the jaw rather than between the jaws. Align yaw so the jaw axis runs roughly along the lobe's long axis (crest ridge direction), i.e. the jaw slides parallel to the roll and under it, which is the complement of iteration 31's perpendicular crest straddle; stage 2 should hold one constant yaw with no wrist rotation during translation. Close the gripper at that threaded pose, then perform purely vertical lift checkpoints at about +20 mm and +35 mm with requires_lift_checkpoint=true, so any hooked cloth must tent or rise. No post-close lateral transport and no laydown this iteration. Reverse strictly: lower back to the exact contact pose, release, withdraw the fingertip back out along the identical entry line to zero net lateral displacement, retreat vertically, and home. Intended eventual transport direction once acquisition is validated is image-left sleeve inward toward the chest-print centre, a useful distance on the order of the sleeve's own reach (roughly the shoulder-to-cuff span), but that transport is deferred and not part of this probe.
decision.expected_observation: Discriminating outcome at the +20 mm and +35 mm checkpoints. Positive: the Camera C hold-check shows the rolled lobe deformed upward — local tenting, a cone of fabric drawn up under the fingertips, the crest lifting or the lobe tip peeling off the table — even if the jaws never mechanically arrest, which would show cloth is capturable by hooking and would refute pure closure-actuation failure as a total blocker. Negative: table remains visible beneath and beside the jaws, the collar, print, image-right sleeve and bottom hem stay flat and seated, and no tile shows cloth following the jaws up; combined with iteration 31's clean refutation under sound grounding, depth and entry, that would leave closure actuation as the confirmed blocker and mean no admissible planner-side geometric change remains, so the host must answer whether any parameterised, force-limited or partial close exists before further probing is informative. Third possible outcome: the fingertip fails to enter beneath the rim and instead ploughs the lobe inboard, visible as the lobe shifting toward the print — that would indicate the arch is not a genuine void and the relief is compacted rather than hollow. Because the probe is strictly zero-net-lateral with release at the exact contact pose, the after-state should otherwise match the before-state.
safety_notes: Reversible probe only: release at the exact contact pose and retrace the identical entry line so net lateral displacement is zero and the garment stays recoverable for the ordered five-step fold.

proposal.garment_observation:
Canonical upright Camera A shows the black short-sleeve T-shirt fully unfolded on the pale table: collar and white neck label at top-centre, pixel-art chest print filling the torso, bottom hem open and flat, no fold ply overlapping anywhere. The image-right sleeve lies extended as flat single ply; the image-left sleeve, the named target, is gathered into a compact rolled lobe with standing relief at the far image-left of the shoulder. Empty completed_steps and current_step = left_sleeve are correct.

The committed measurement does not land on that lobe. A/R030 returned base (630.83, 34.26) at pixel (599, 359), table_z 61.55 mm, height_above_table 2.27 mm. That is 257.9 mm from the Molmo image-left sleeve hint (573.05, -217.07), failing the historical 40 mm sleeve gate by 217.9 mm, and it sits on the positive-y side of the garment centreline while the left sleeve sits near y -213. It is only 83.5 mm from the validated torso centre (589.75, -38.46), so it is flat upper-torso / image-right-shoulder ply, not left-sleeve fabric. Pixel row 359 is six 48 px strides from the row-647 band whose hold-checks confirmed sleeve contact in iterations 17, 18, 20, 22, 29 and 31 — the same stride re-index signature already recorded for R082, R087 and R074.

Stage 1 named this exact failure mode and specified substituting an adjacent in-gate marker in the far-left lobe cluster. lookup_budget_remaining is 0, so no re-selection is possible, and I will not fabricate a sleeve coordinate that no lookup returned. This is the tenth iteration whose region credit is lost this way.
proposal.reveal_strategy:
Disclosed before execution: this probe cannot test the image-left sleeve. A/R030 measured 257.9 mm from the Molmo sleeve hint, across the garment centreline in y, and 83.5 mm from the validated torso centre, so the contact will land on flat upper-torso / image-right-shoulder ply. left_sleeve cannot be credited whatever happens, exactly as in iterations 21, 23 and 26. I am honouring the 2 mm anchor rule rather than inventing an in-gate coordinate, because the single lookup is spent.

The intended rolling/buckling bite — closing while translating — is the one structurally untried experiment left, but this iteration's ACQUISITION PROBE contract mandates requires_lift_checkpoint=true, which forbids closure during translation. The objective file is authoritative, so that experiment is deferred and requires_lift_checkpoint stays true.

What this iteration can still settle is region-independent and is currently the live dispute: whether sub-plane depth should be commanded as a per-frame relative offset or as an absolute Z. Iteration 28 loaded fabric at z 45.0 with table_z 51.55 (-6.55 mm). Iterations 29, 30 and 31 reproduced that relative offset at z 46-48 and loaded nothing. This frame reports table_z 61.55 mm, the highest of the run, so plane-minus-6.55 mm here is z 55.0 — about 10 mm higher in absolute Z than every prior loading attempt. A 26 mm open-jaw sub-plane sweep at z 55.0 therefore discriminates the two rules directly: visible drag supports the relative rule, a null supports a true plane near 45-48 mm absolute and marks iteration 28 as an absolute-Z artefact.

Structure kept from prior iterations: single constant yaw 0 at every waypoint, staged transit at z 120 and z 80, no wrist rotation during translation, jaws opened clear before descent, two purely vertical post-close lifts at +20 and +35 mm, release at the exact contact pose, retrace of the identical sweep line outboard, zero net lateral displacement.

Standing requests, twenty-seventh consecutive: state definitively whether any parameterised, force-limited or partial close exists, since close_gripper accepts only an empty args object; raise the lookup budget above one call or enforce the sleeve gate host-side; and provide an instrumented touch-down recording height at first contact, which the 16 mm table_z spread now makes a precondition for any further depth reasoning.

Primary readout is region-independent and is about depth, not the sleeve.

If the per-frame relative rule holds: the before/after Camera C stills differ at the upper-torso/image-right shoulder region, with fabric visibly dragged or rucked along the 26 mm inboard sweep line, reproducing iteration 28's signature at a 10 mm higher absolute Z. That would establish that plane-minus-6.5-mm tracks the true cloth plane per frame and would make table_z usable despite the 45-62 mm spread.

If nothing moves: combined with iterations 29-31, this argues the true plane sits near 45-48 mm absolute regardless of the reported table_z, so iteration 28 loaded cloth because of its low absolute Z rather than its relative offset. Either result constrains the next well-grounded sleeve probe.

Acquisition itself is expected to be null again, at both the +20 mm (z 75) and +35 mm (z 90) checkpoints: pale table visible between and below the jaws, collar, print, both sleeves and hem seated, nothing suspended in any contact-sheet tile. Thirty-two closes will have driven position_pulse 850 to 0 with mechanical_grasp_detected false.

Regardless of outcome, do not score this against left_sleeve contact geometry and do not credit any sub-action: completed_steps stays empty and current_step stays left_sleeve. The well-grounded sleeve tests remain iterations 14, 17, 18, 20, 22, 24, 27, 29 and 31.

decision.garment_observation:
Canonical upright Camera A shows a black short-sleeve T-shirt lying fully unfolded on a pale table: collar and white neck label at top-centre, pixel-art (Minecraft face grid) chest print filling the torso centre, bottom hem open and unlifted. No fold ply overlaps anywhere — the print is entirely unobscured — so no sleeve and no torso side has been laid inward. Consistent with empty completed_steps and current_step = left_sleeve.

The image-right sleeve extends outboard to the upper right as a clean flat single-ply lobe. The image-left sleeve, the named target, is different: rather than lying extended flat it is gathered into a compact rolled/curled lobe at the far image-left of the shoulder, with a visible standing crest and a curled free edge facing outboard toward the table. This lobe is the only region with genuine off-plane relief; the rest reads as a single low-relief sheet. The Molmo sleeve-region hint falls on this lobe, corroborating it as left-sleeve fabric, not torso, print, label, or opposite sleeve.

One discrepancy with the supervisor text: the loose rumple is at the image-left sleeve/shoulder, not near the hem; the hem looks flat. Frame clutter (a lamp head and a tripod/stand) sits below and left of the garment, outside the mask but inside the workspace view.
decision.opening_strategy:
Objective unchanged: bring the image-left sleeve inward across the chest. This iteration is a reversible acquisition probe under the execution contract, not the fold, because acquisition has never been validated (28 attempts, 25 consecutive nulls).

Saved physical evidence closes nearly the whole static geometric space at this sleeve. Iterations 14-31 covered interior mid-lobe ply, edge-crossing lines, corner straddle, off-cloth edge capture, throat capture by sweep, wedge under the free edge, cuff double ply, seam-band relief, pure vertical arrival, sub-plane scrub/scoop/gathering stroke and top-down crest straddle, at yaw -75 through +90. Iteration 31 was the cleanest — sound lobe grounding, vertical entry, sub-plane depth, yaw across the crest ridges — and still returned nothing. A thirty-second static permutation, or changing only grasp Z, is inadmissible and uninformative.

The one structurally untried non-height contact change the contract still permits is closure timing: close while the jaw is still translating so a bow of the rolled sleeve tube buckles ahead of the advancing finger and is trapped in the throat, instead of closing on halted flat-seated ply where the finger exterior ploughs cloth aside. The rolled left-sleeve lobe is the ideal substrate because it already stands off the plane and can buckle rather than flatten.

So: hold the two supported variables (well-grounded lobe band nearest the Molmo hint, shallow sub-plane depth), shift contact XY only slightly to sit just outboard of the lobe crest, and make closure-during-motion plus the short pre-close inboard sweep the sole new experiment. Nothing is transported and no fold is credited.

decision.motion_intent:
Reversible probe only, no post-close lateral transport.

1) Transit high above the garment, staged descent (high, then intermediate) at a single constant yaw with no wrist rotation during translation, arriving over a point just outboard (image-left / table side) of the rolled sleeve lobe crest — never over the print or opposite sleeve.
2) Open jaws fully before descent so fingertips are clear of cloth.
3) Descend near-vertically to a fingertip depth a few millimetres below the current best table-plane estimate, matching the shallow sub-plane offset that first loaded fabric in iteration 28, and no deeper. Depth is held constant; it is not the variable.
4) Yaw: orient the finger pair so the closing axis is perpendicular to the intended travel and the jaw line runs roughly parallel to the lobe crest ridge (upper-left to lower-right in the upright frame), with the open throat facing inboard, so an advancing bow enters the throat instead of being swept aside.
5) With jaws still open, translate a short distance inboard toward the shoulder/print side, roughly 20-30 mm, so cloth buckles ahead of the throat, and command the close mid-travel near the anchor rather than from a halted pose. This is the sole new variable.
6) requires_lift_checkpoint = true: two purely vertical lift checkpoints (about +20 mm then +35 mm), zero lateral component, each with a hold-check witness still.
7) Reverse: open jaws, retrace the identical inboard travel back outboard to the exact entry pose, ascend along the same vertical line, return home. Net lateral displacement zero; garment left recoverable.

Positive case: at the +20 mm and +35 mm checkpoints the hold-check still shows the rolled left-sleeve lobe following the jaws — local tenting or a cone of fabric drawn up under the fingertips, table visible beneath the lifted cloth — while collar, print, image-right sleeve and hem stay seated. That would identify closure timing (bite on a moving buckle) as the missing variable and license the next iteration to expand into the real left_sleeve fold: grasp at the same band and transport inboard toward the print centre, roughly 150-200 mm, then lay the sleeve down over the chest.

Negative case: pale table again visible between and below the jaws at both checkpoints, nothing suspended in any contact-sheet tile, garment unchanged. With grounding on the lobe, sub-plane depth, and closure during motion on standing relief, a null would exhaust the planner-visible space of contact XY, jaw alignment, entry path and closure timing. The correct response is then to stop probing geometry and require a host answer on whether any parameterised, force-limited or partial close exists, plus an instrumented touch-down height, given the twenty-plus inconsistent table_z estimates (45-61 mm).

Either way completed_steps stays empty and current_step stays left_sleeve.
safety_notes: Strictly reversible: release at the exact contact pose and retrace the identical inboard travel and vertical line; net lateral displacement must be zero and no fold laydown is permitted this iteration.

Sub-plane fingertip depth risks table contact. Go only a few millimetres below the current best plane estimate, never deeper than iteration 28's offset, and abort on any controller force, torque or joint-limit report.

evidence: Acquisition-only evaluation did not reassess semantic target selection.

The Camera C lift hold-check still, captured immediately after the first post-close lift to z 75, shows the gripper shaft and jaw assembly standing in clear air above the upper-right/shoulder side of the garment with pale background and the white mount plate visible between and below the jaws; no black cloth patch is pinched or hanging from the fingertips.

In that same hold-check the collar, chest print grid, both sleeve lobes and the bottom hem all remain flat and seated on the table, and there is no local tenting, peaking or cone of fabric drawn up beneath the fingertips.

Across all 16 Camera C contact-sheet tiles the garment silhouette is unchanged from tile 1 to tile 16; the arm descends and withdraws at the upper/right region (tiles 6-12) and no tile shows cloth following the jaws upward at either the +20 mm (z 75) or +35 mm (z 90) checkpoint.

Host telemetry corroborates rather than conflicts: position_pulse runs 850 to 0 at the close with no arrest, mechanical_grasp_detected is false at every post-close boundary, and no sample reports state=grasp, so there is no mechanical contact signal to weigh against the visual null.

The intended structure was any ply beneath the jaws driven into the throat by a 26 mm sub-plane open-jaw inboard sweep at yaw 0. The hold-check shows no independent cloth patch elevated with the gripper and no local tenting under the fingertips, so neither the named sleeve nor the substituted torso ply was acquired.

The named image-left sleeve was never contacted. A/R030 measured (630.83, 34.26), 257.9 mm from the Molmo image-left sleeve hint and on the positive-y side of the centreline while the left sleeve lobe sits near y -213; the hold-check places the jaws at the upper-torso/right-shoulder side of the garment.

The rolled image-left sleeve lobe is visibly unchanged in the hold-check and in every contact-sheet tile: its gathered crest and curled outboard tip remain seated on the table, confirming no cloth was drawn from the target region.

The designed secondary readout also came back negative: no ruck, drag or pucker appears anywhere along the 26 mm sweep line at z 55.0, so the sub-plane sweep did not load fabric at this frame's plane-minus-6.55 mm depth.
Transport was intentionally not executed in the reversible acquisition probe.
The probe reversed and released at the original contact instead of laying down a fold.

metrics.boundary_change: The compact evaluator directly reported no persistent garment-state change.

keep: current_step left_sleeve and the empty ordered five-step ledger: nothing was grasped, transported or folded, and the contact was not on the named sleeve, so no sub-action can be credited.
The strictly reversible zero-net-lateral probe structure with release at the exact contact pose and retrace of the identical sweep line outboard, which again left the garment recoverable.
requires_lift_checkpoint true with purely vertical post-close lifts at +20 mm and +35 mm, directly comparable with iterations 7, 8 and 10-31.
Use of the Camera C hold-check still as the authoritative acquisition witness, with the simulated telemetry as corroboration only.
The single-constant-yaw path-shaping rule with staged transit at z 120 and z 80 and no wrist rotation during translation, which again produced a controller-valid path.

Advance disclosure of the 217.9 mm sleeve-gate failure, of the spent lookup budget, and of the explicit refusal to fabricate an in-gate sleeve coordinate. That candour is what makes this negative interpretable rather than ambiguous.
change: Do not score this iteration against left_sleeve contact geometry, and do not count it as a geometric permutation. A/R030 measured (630.83, 34.26) at pixel (599,359): 257.9 mm from the Molmo image-left sleeve hint, on the opposite side of the garment centreline in y, and only 83.5 mm from the validated torso centre. The hold-check independently places the jaws at the upper-torso/right-shoulder side. The well-grounded sleeve tests remain iterations 14, 17, 18, 20, 22, 24, 27, 29 and 31.

Record the depth result, which is the one substantive and region-independent finding. The 26 mm open-jaw sweep at z 55.0, commanded 6.55 mm below this frame's table_z of 61.55 mm, produced no visible drag, ruck or displacement anywhere along its line. Iteration 28 loaded fabric at z 45.0; iterations 29, 30, 31 and now 33 reproduced the same relative offset at z 46-55 and loaded nothing. The per-frame relative rule is therefore not supported: the true cloth plane appears to sit near 45-48 mm absolute, and iteration 28's load is better explained by its low absolute Z than by plane-minus-6.5-mm. Command absolute Z near 45 mm in future probes rather than a relative offset from the reported table_z.

Fix the reference grounding defect host-side before spending another probe; this is the tenth iteration lost to it. Pixel row 359 is six 48 px strides from the row-647 band that produced witness-confirmed sleeve landings, the same stride re-index signature already logged for R082, R087 and R074. Either raise the lookup budget above one call so a mis-grounded measurement can be re-selected, or enforce the sleeve proximity gate host-side before the anchor is committed. Under the current single-call budget plus the 2 mm anchor rule, a bad measurement guarantees a wasted iteration.

Run the closure-during-translation experiment, which remains the only structurally untried non-height change and has now been deferred four consecutive times. It needs requires_lift_checkpoint=false, which this iteration's ACQUISITION PROBE contract forbade, so the host must issue a contract that permits it. It should be run at the row-647 sleeve band and at absolute z near 45 mm so closure timing is the sole new variable.

Answer definitively whether any parameterised, force-limited or partial close exists, twenty-seventh consecutive escalation. Thirty-two closes have now driven position_pulse 850 to 0 with no arrest and mechanical_grasp_detected false, and close_gripper accepts only an empty args object, so jaw width, pinch force, closure speed and partial-close width cannot be commanded. If none exists, say so explicitly so the strategy stops assuming one may appear.

Provide an instrumented touch-down recording height at first contact, or state definitively that it is unavailable. table_z 61.55 mm is the twenty-first mutually inconsistent estimate and now the highest of the run (spread 45.08-61.55 mm), and height_above_table 2.27 mm here versus 14-35 mm on comparable flat ply in recent frames cannot all be right. Depth reasoning cannot advance on this signal.
