Canonical upright Camera A shows the black short-sleeve T-shirt still fully unfolded on the pale table, unchanged from iteration 33 as a reversible probe implies: collar and white neck label at top-centre, pixel-art chest print filling the torso entirely unobscured, bottom hem open and flat, no fold ply overlapping anywhere. Empty completed_steps with current_step = left_sleeve is correct.

The image-right sleeve extends outboard as flat single ply. The image-left sleeve, the named target, is the garment's only region with genuine off-plane relief: gathered into a compact rolled tube at the far image-left of the shoulder, axis running upper-right to lower-left, ending in a thickened knot at the outboard tip with a curled free edge facing the table.

Grounding is sound this iteration, unlike the last. A/R087 returned base (598.95, -222.18) at pixel (591, 647), table_z 49.52 mm, height_above_table 9.52 mm. That sits 26.4 mm from the Molmo image-left sleeve hint (573.05, -217.07), inside the 40 mm gate, and 183.5 mm from the validated torso centre (590.99, -38.86), so it is left-sleeve fabric and not torso, print, label or opposite sleeve. Pixel row 647 is the band whose hold-checks confirmed sleeve contact in iterations 17, 18, 20, 22, 29 and 31, with no stride re-index this time. The measurement lies 35.4 mm outboard along that band from iteration 31's confirmed landing (564.84, -212.89), which places it at the tip knot rather than the lobe body — the intended new contact XY. The 9.52 mm height_above_table is the largest relief reading recorded on this band and is consistent with the standing rolled tube seen in RGB.
proposal.reveal_strategy:
This is a reversible acquisition probe, not the fold: acquisition has never validated in 29 attempts with 26 consecutive failures, so no transport or laydown is included.

Two corrections from iteration 33 are carried in. Grounding: that iteration was lost because its reference measured 257.9 mm from the Molmo hint on the far side of the centreline and tested upper torso instead of the sleeve. R087 passes the combined gate-plus-reproducibility test here at 26.4 mm from the hint on the confirmed row-647 band, so the region is sound before execution rather than argued after it. Depth: iteration 33 showed the per-frame relative rule fails — a sweep at plane-minus-6.55 mm but absolute z 55.0 moved nothing, while iteration 28 loaded fabric at absolute z 45.0, and iterations 29-31 at comparable relative offsets (z 46-48) did not. I therefore command absolute z 45.0 rather than an offset from this frame's table_z. Against this frame's reported plane of 49.52 mm that happens to be 4.52 mm sub-plane, but the absolute value is the reasoned choice and it is not deeper than iteration 28's.

The non-height changes that make this a new experiment are contact XY and jaw alignment. Contact moves 35.4 mm outboard along the confirmed band onto the thickened tip knot of the rolled tube, where standing relief is greatest (9.52 mm here versus the implausible 24-35 mm readings on flat ply in recent frames). Yaw -55 sets the closing axis across the tube's long axis so the fingers land on its flanks and pinch across it; iteration 31's -40 crossed the crest ridges on the lobe body, not the tip knot across its axis. Entry is purely vertical with zero lateral component, so nothing is ploughed.

Stated plainly: the experiment the last four evaluators asked for — closure during translation, a rolling bite on a moving bow — is deferred for a fifth time because it requires requires_lift_checkpoint=false and this iteration's ACQUISITION PROBE contract mandates true. I am not disguising a permutation as that experiment. If this probe also returns null, the planner-side space under a halted close is exhausted and the host must either permit closure-during-translation or state definitively that no parameterised, force-limited or partial close exists. That question is now at its twenty-eighth consecutive escalation: thirty-two closes have driven position_pulse 850 to 0 with no arrest and mechanical_grasp_detected false, and close_gripper accepts only an empty args object. An instrumented touch-down recording height at first contact remains needed; table_z has now returned 22 mutually inconsistent values spanning 45.08 to 61.55 mm.
proposal.expected_observation:
Positive: at the +20 mm (z 65) and +35 mm (z 80) checkpoints the Camera C hold-check shows the rolled sleeve tip knot lifted with the jaws — a black bundle held clear with table visible beneath it — while collar, print, image-right sleeve and hem stay seated. That would be the run's first validated acquisition and would license the next iteration to expand into the actual left_sleeve fold: same anchor, transport inboard toward the print centre roughly 150-200 mm, then lay the sleeve across the chest.

Negative: pale table again visible between and below the jaws at both checkpoints, nothing suspended in any of the 16 contact-sheet tiles, garment unchanged. This probe combines sound grounding on the confirmed row-647 band, the thickest standing relief on the garment, corrected absolute depth, purely vertical entry and an across-tube pinch, so a null cannot be attributed to region, aim, relief, depth or entry path. It would leave closure timing as the only untested planner-visible variable and closure actuation as the blocker.

Secondary readout, independent of whether anything is gripped: whether absolute z 45.0 reproduces iteration 28's visible cloth drag at this band. Confirmation would settle the absolute-versus-relative depth question that iteration 33 opened.

Either way, do not credit any sub-action: completed_steps stays empty and current_step stays left_sleeve.

No substitution was needed and none is available: lookup_budget_remaining is 0.

Commanded z 45.0 is an absolute depth, not deeper than iteration 28's loading value, and 4.52 mm below this frame's reported table_z of 49.52 mm. Abort on any controller force, torque or joint-limit report.

4) Descend purely vertically, entry_lateral zero, to an absolute depth near 45 mm rather than a relative offset from this frame's reported table_z. evaluation_raw.prompt:
ACQUISITION-PROBE EVALUATION ONLY. This robot action closed the gripper, made two short lift checkpoints, then reversed to the original contact and released. Inspect only the labelled RGB files and chronological rollout contact sheets below. Decide whether cloth visibly followed and remained supported by the gripper during the lift, and whether the intended local garment structure rather than empty space or whole-garment drag was acquired. Do not evaluate fold transport, laydown, final garment shape, or overall task progress. Never infer success from the command. The next_experiment decision must be causal: after an empty close, consider contact XY, jaw alignment, pre-close entry path, closure geometry, and Z as competing hypotheses; after repeated similar failures, include a non-height contact change. Do not name a privileged grasp solution without visible evidence. Also report whether the garment's persistent after-state visibly changed; use UNKNOWN when the RGB is ambiguous. Return exactly the compact JSON schema.

The host xArm telemetry is an independent mechanical signal. A sample with state=grasp (status low bits=2) after close and during/after lift is positive evidence that the gripper controller detected an object. It is not proof that the object is the intended sleeve, and it can be triggered by a table/obstacle. If telemetry says grasp while the target is fully occluded in the video, do not call it a visual empty grasp: use SUCCESS when the mechanical evidence is consistent, or UNKNOWN when it conflicts with visible contact. Do not use an unchanged after image to negate a reversible probe, because the probe intentionally returns and releases at the original pose.

Camera C is an uncalibrated side observer. Use its RGB/video only for visual occlusion and cloth-motion evidence; never infer depth, pixels, or robot coordinates from it. A still labelled as a Camera C lift hold-check was captured immediately after the first post-close lift action and is the primary acquisition witness. If it shows an independent sleeve patch elevated with the gripper, classify grasp_acquisition as SUCCESS even if the reversible probe later releases and the final after image is unchanged.

evidence: Acquisition-only evaluation did not reassess semantic target selection.

The Camera C hold-check still, captured immediately after the first post-close lift to z 65, is materially different from every prior iteration in this run: a black cloth mass is gathered hard against the closed jaw assembly at the image-left sleeve/shoulder region, rising vertically from the table into the fingertips, instead of the pale table and background that were visible between and below the jaws in iterations 27-31 and 33.

The engagement is not clearly an independent suspended patch, which is why this is not scored SUCCESS: no pale table is visible underneath the gathered mass, and the cloth remains contiguous with the seated garment, so the still is equally consistent with fabric tented and dragged upward under the fingers as with a ply pinched and supported clear of the surface.

The contact sheet corroborates real engagement rather than a viewpoint artefact: tiles 5-12 show the arm descending at the image-left region, and from tile 9 onward the image-left shoulder silhouette is visibly altered, with the sleeve mass pulled inboard and standing higher than in tiles 1-4, where it lay as a low rolled lobe.

Host telemetry conflicts with the visual engagement and is the reason for UNKNOWN rather than SUCCESS: position_pulse runs 850 to 0 at the close with no arrest, mechanical_grasp_detected is false at every post-close boundary, and no sample reports state=grasp, so the controller registered no object while the video shows cloth loaded against the jaws.

The intended structure was the thickened knot at the outboard tip of the rolled image-left sleeve tube, pinched across its long axis at yaw -55 by a purely vertical descent to absolute z 45.0. The hold-check shows cloth gathered against the jaws at exactly that region, so the contact was on the named target rather than torso, print, label or opposite sleeve.

Grounding supports the region claim independently of the image: A/R087 measured (598.95, -222.18) at pixel (591,647), 26.4 mm from the Molmo image-left sleeve hint and inside the 40 mm gate, 183.5 mm from the validated torso centre, on the row-647 band whose hold-checks confirmed sleeve contact in iterations 17, 18, 20, 22, 29 and 31, with no stride re-index this frame.

Whether the named structure was acquired rather than merely disturbed cannot be settled from these stills: the gathered mass is contiguous with the seated garment with no pale table visible beneath it, so a pinched sleeve ply and a cone of tented fabric under the fingertips are both consistent with the evidence.

The rest of the garment is unambiguous and rules out whole-garment drag: collar, neck label, chest print grid, image-right sleeve and bottom hem remain flat and seated in the hold-check and across all 16 contact-sheet tiles, so any engagement was local to the left sleeve lobe.
Transport was intentionally not executed in the reversible acquisition probe.
The probe reversed and released at the original contact instead of laying down a fold.

keep: current_step left_sleeve and the empty ordered five-step ledger: no transport or laydown occurred and the hold is unconfirmed, so no sub-action can be credited.
The strictly reversible zero-net-lateral probe structure with release at the exact contact pose and a retreat retracing the identical vertical line, which again left the garment recoverable.
requires_lift_checkpoint true with purely vertical post-close lifts, keeping the hold-check comparable with iterations 7, 8 and 10-33.
Use of the Camera C hold-check still as the authoritative acquisition witness, with the simulated telemetry as corroboration only.
The single-constant-yaw path-shaping rule with staged transit at z 120 and z 80 and no wrist rotation during translation, which again produced a controller-valid path.

A/R087 at pixel (591,647) as the best-grounded sleeve anchor of the run: 26.4 mm from the Molmo hint, inside the 40 mm gate, 183.5 mm from the validated torso centre, on the row band with six prior confirmed sleeve landings, and with the largest relief reading recorded on that band.
change: Score this as the first probe in the run to produce unambiguous cloth engagement at the named target, and treat that as the substantive result. The combination that produced it was new on two non-height axes: contact XY moved 35.4 mm outboard along the confirmed row-647 band onto the thickened tip knot of the rolled tube (598.95, -222.18 versus iteration 31's 564.84, -212.89), and yaw -55 pinched across the tube's long axis rather than crossing crest ridges on the lobe body. Retain both.

Resolve the lift-versus-tent ambiguity as the single next question, because it is now the only thing separating this from a validated acquisition. Add a third, higher vertical checkpoint (roughly +60 to +80 mm) to the same probe at the same anchor, yaw and depth. Cloth that is genuinely pinched will remain with the jaws and show pale table beneath it at that height; cloth that is merely tented will drop away and reseat. This is a checkpoint-height change, not a new contact hypothesis, so the contact geometry stays frozen as the control.

Treat the telemetry-versus-video conflict as a measurement defect to be fixed rather than evidence of failure. mechanical_grasp_detected is false while the video shows cloth loaded against the jaws, and all eleven samples remain simulated:true sharing a single timestamp (09:09:58.016), as in every prior iteration. State whether this feedback path is mechanically live at all; if it is simulated end-to-end it cannot adjudicate acquisition and should stop being reported as an independent signal.

Record the depth result: absolute z 45.0 did engage cloth, reproducing iteration 28's absolute value, whereas iterations 29, 30, 31 and 33 at relative plane-minus-5-to-6.5-mm offsets (z 46-55) did not. Two of two engagements now occur at absolute z 45 and five of five nulls at higher absolute Z. Command absolute z near 45 mm and abandon the per-frame relative offset rule. This frame's table_z of 49.52 mm is the twenty-second inconsistent estimate in a 45.08-61.55 mm spread.

Keep the grounding discipline that made this iteration interpretable and make it host-enforced. R087 measured 26.4 mm from the Molmo hint, inside the 40 mm gate, on pixel row 647 with six prior witness-confirmed sleeve landings and no stride re-index. Enforce that gate host-side before the anchor is committed, or raise the lookup budget above one call, so a re-index cannot waste an iteration as it did in 33.

Do not yet expand to transport and laydown. If the added high checkpoint confirms the ply is genuinely held, the following iteration may expand at this exact anchor, yaw and depth: lift clear, transport inboard toward the print centre roughly 150-200 mm, and lay the sleeve across the chest. Expanding before that confirmation risks dragging the whole garment from a tented contact.

I therefore command absolute z 45.0 rather than an offset from this frame's table_z.
